description:
What if the key to quieting your inner critic isn’t pushing harder, but choosing joy? In this powerful talk, Olympian Lisa Weagle invites us to rethink our definitions of success and self-worth. She shares tools that helped her discover joy and fulfillment, not just in the podium moments, but in the journey itself. 

Lisa Weagle is a two-time Olympian, world champion, and one of Canada’s most respected curling athletes, having spent over 15 years competing at the highest levels of sport. Recently retired from competition, she is the founder of the Lisa Weagle Curling Academy, where she coaches the next generation of high-performance youth athletes. Drawing on her experiences of competing on the world stage, Lisa’s TEDx talk explores how we can quiet the inner critic by reframing joy not as a result, but as a mindset that shapes how we experience challenge and success. title: 3 ways to be less hard on yourself | Lisa Weagle | TEDxMechanicsville

description:
With unprecedented advancements in medicine, communication, and space exploration, we seem to be on the cusp of conquering the universe. Yet, despite these accomplishments, humanity remains mired in wars, poverty, and human suffering.

Drawing from his own experiences, Dr. Nemat asks: What is the true cost of progress? He traces the history of the 20th century, marked by devastating wars and political repression, highlighting how science and technology have been used both to uplift and to destroy. In this thought-provoking talk, he urges us to reimagine progress—not as the mere accumulation of knowledge or power, but as the pursuit of empathy, justice, and peace. With wisdom from Rumi and Saadi, Dr. Nemat challenges us to question whether our advancements are truly advancing humanity, or merely leading us down a destructive path.

This talk is a call to action for the youth, thinkers, and dreamers of today to shape a world where knowledge is anchored in compassion, where technology se
title: The homecoming of humanity | Dr. Arash Nemat | TEDxAsmayee

Sangieta Bhatia is a communication coach dedicated to helping individuals discover their voice and speak with clarity, confidence, and purpose. In this inspiring TEDx talk, Jasmine Williams shares the transformative journey she experienced while walking the Camino de Santiago, a historic pilgrimage across northern Spain. Through rugged terrain, early mornings, and moments of both solitude and connection, Jasmine reflects on the unexpected lessons the path taught her about resilience, presence, and what it truly means to learn from life itself.

As she walked hundreds of miles with only what she could carry, Jasmine discovered that the deepest insights often come not from textbooks or classes, but from lived experience, community, and inner reflection. Her story invites us all to embrace discomfort, slow down, and open ourselves to the wisdom that comes only through walking our own paths.

title: Lessons from the Camino de Santiago | Jasmine Williams | TEDxOvertown

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) could become either the greatest equalizer or the greatest divider of our time. In this talk, the speaker reflects on growing up in Bangladesh, where electricity was once a luxury, and contrasts that reality with today's global race for AI.

He argues that the world may soon face a new divide-not between countries, but between “AI-rich” and “AI-poor” nations. Building advanced AI requires massive compute power, data centers, energy, and specialized talent, resources currently concentrated in only a few places. Without deliberate action, developing countries risk becoming permanent consumers of AI rather than creators of it.

However, the speaker also highlights an opportunity. Just as many developing countries leapfrogged landlines with smartphones and traditional banking with mobile money, AI could offer a chance to leapfrog again-if nations act strategically.

He proposes six key strategies for developing countries: building national compute infrastructu
title: AI for the Poor: The New Global Divide | Hasnaeen Rizvi Rahman | TEDxNorthSouthUniversity

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if doing everything “right” still leads to failure?

In this TEDx talk, Akshay Goel challenges the traditional belief that strong résumés and online applications are the key to career success. Despite an exceptional academic and professional profile, he shares how he faced repeated rejection, until a single insight changed his approach.

Drawing from years of experience across technology, strategy, and career coaching, this talk introduces the idea of the silent job market, the opportunities that never appear on job portals and are filled through conversations, networks, and trust. Akshay explains why most candidates unknowingly compete in overcrowded systems, and how shifting from applications to authentic engagement can transform outcomes.

This talk invites us to rethink how opportunity really works, and where success actually begins. Akshay Goel is a Wall Street Journal and USA Today bestselling author, keynote speaker, and startup advisor who helps experts build authority an
title: Why your Résumé won’t land you a Job | Akshay Goel | TEDxDDUC

author: TEDx Talks
description: Samad Shoeb challenges the belief that degrees alone create success. Drawing from history, psychology, leadership training, and real world observation, he reveals the invisible force that has shaped kings, empires, and modern leaders alike the power of voice, presence, and personality. From Chanakya and Buddha to Napoleon and today’s global icons, Samad shows why influence has always mattered more than intelligence or marks. In an era where artificial intelligence can generate information but not conviction, his talk delivers a powerful message to students and young leaders alike the future belongs to those who can express ideas clearly, move minds, and make others believe. The crown, he reminds us, was never external it was always within your voice. Samad Shoeb is the CEO of Oratrics, empowering students, professionals, and C-suite leaders to communicate with charisma and evolve into their greatest selves, and is known for combining leadership coaching with impactful public speaking
title: The Hidden Skill That Has Ruled the World for Thousands of Years | Samad Shoeb | TEDxDDUC

description:
In this remarkable 96 year old's first TED Talk, at the age of 87, she shared how "It's Never Too Late".  

In this Talk she shares her 4 most important secrets for staying young . . . in order to do more of the things you want to do in your life.  

Secret #1 will surprise many, but prominent Neuroscientists believe it is the #1 brain activity for seniors . . . PING PONG.  And Eileen plays almost every day!
Secret #2 for Eileen is a disciplined, largely plant-based diet.  And she really keeps to it!
Secret #3, unsurprisingly for this Certified Hypnotherapist, is a Positive Mindset. She doesn't do negativity!
And Secret #4 is a call to action for all "Elders" to share their well-earned wisdom . . . and give back as a key purpose of their life.

Music is his comfort zone—singing his favourite songs helps him feel calm and confident. He treasures his family and stands by his friends with care and kindness.

description: Aparna reflects on how a painting about the Kerala floods revealed the power of perspective in art. Through this journey, she realises that art is not about perfection or marks, but about perspective, freedom, and human connection. Aparna is a student  with a rooted passion for giving back to society. With so many aspects of our lives seemingly spiraling beyond our control, Aparna often finds herself reflecting on moments where people came together in solitude, from fear to fire, to spark the flames of hope that shine bright even in the darkest of times. In this talk, Jaci shares how her journey as an athlete, Native woman, and founder of the influential nonprofit, Rise Above which has led her to build a movement that helps Native youth see themselves differently. Not through the limits placed on them, but through purpose, power, and possibility. Her message is a compelling reminder that when young people can see themselves reflected in leadership, they can begin to imagine entirely new futures. Rise Above, empowers Native youth through sports, education, mentorship, and prevention-based programs.
